notes: No convincing localized trigger circuit found. Embedding norm median/p99/max = 0.547/0.934/1.208 (maximum token 162); the largest row is not orders of magnitude larger than peers. Classifier row norms span 1.708-1.999 and absolute bias is at most 0.139. MLP spectra are distributed and neuron input/output norms show no dominant isolated unit. Attention head 1 OV is concentrated (top singular energy 0.954), but its operator norm is 0.267 and its raw token-class path maximum 0.141 versus p99 0.115; multiple tokens contribute rather than one exceptional trigger. Head 0 OV operator norm is 0.0153. QK bilinear analyses including query bias and positional directions show broad key preferences, not a singleton universal attractor. LayerNorm-gain/centering-aware paths also show no exceptional singleton. Token 162 maximizes the scaled direct path, but unit-embedding score 3.604 is close to p99 3.524, and its direct and linear MLP maxima target different classes. Earlier positional embeddings are nearly parallel (cosines 0.993-0.996); their norms are about 1 versus 0.093 at the last position, compatible with positional specialization rather than a position-0 trigger. These are within-checkpoint descriptive comparisons, not calibration against clean reference checkpoints or an empirical null. Confidence is a subjective audit judgment. Virtual paths omit data-dependent LayerNorm denominators, GELU gating, attention softmax, and nonlinear interactions; they are not logits or behavioral verification. Zero forward passes, no sequences, no training, and no edits. A subtle nonlinear backdoor cannot be excluded.

evidence.calibration: Within-checkpoint distributions only; no reference ensemble or behavioral validation
